api-errors.reason: ThalovantApiError.httpFailure in Sources/ThalovantSDK/Errors.swift, which every non-2xx answer ThalovantControlPlane.requestData receives goes through, parses the body once into problem, errorCode and the whole detail, and leaves the bounded message as it was. Run against the shared api-error vectors, each served through URLSession by a URLProtocol with its exact status, Content-Type and body and read back from getHub.

binary.reason: HiveWire.decodeBinaryFrame reads WIRE-1: four bits of payload type, then the clip itself, never parsed or inflated. The Noise framing marks each frame JSON or not and a binary one was refused outright, so every such frame was unreachable; onBinary delivers it now. Run against the shared binary vectors and against binary-frames.json, which is hivemind-bus-client's own encoder output rather than frames this SDK built for itself. A compressed metadata or payload part that is truncated, or would inflate past 32 MiB, refuses the frame rather than reading as empty.

connection-admission.reason: waitForAdmission in Sources/ThalovantSDK/Connections.swift: ready, 404 and no operation are admitted; a 5xx is ridden out, and a 429 for ThalovantApiError.retryAfterSeconds (body, then Retry-After, then RateLimit-Reset); every read is bounded by the deadline and every wait measured on the monotonic clock. failed and timed_out throw ThalovantAdmissionFailedError(errorCode:), any other refusal of the wait the same with the API's answer as apiError; 401/403 pass through as the .auth ThalovantApiError and an API out of reach as .unreachable. The deadline throws ThalovantAdmissionTimeoutError, which conforms to both ThalovantConnectionFailure and ThalovantTimeoutFailure -- Swift's errors are value types, so the two protocols are how it is both -- and ends 'it may still admit it later.'. A links.self on another origin (scheme, host, default-spelled port) is refused unfetched. Run against the shared connection-admission vectors over URLSession, with scripted headers and a real closed loopback port.

connection-kinds.reason: CreateClientIdentityOptions(connectionType:) sends spec.connection_type; createClientIdentity in Sources/ThalovantSDK/ControlPlane.swift checks the echo and, through requireConnectionType in Sources/ThalovantSDK/Connections.swift, deletes a connection made of another kind before failing. Refusals are ThalovantApiError told apart by kind (.unsupportedConnectionType -- a 422 naming the field in its detail, code, or a validation error's loc or msg, never the echoed input -- .plan, .alreadyLinked(clientId:), .auth), read in Sources/ThalovantSDK/Errors.swift. deleteClient reads the etag first, retries once on 412 and counts 404 as deleted. Run against the shared connection-kinds vectors over URLSession.

device-login.reason: beginDeviceLogin, pollDeviceLogin and revokeApiToken in Sources/ThalovantSDK/DeviceLogin.swift, with the per-code interval kept on ThalovantControlPlane and tokenId set by every sign-in from its own answer (keepSignIn in ControlPlane.swift, used by login and by completeNativeSignIn in NativeSignIn.swift). An empty scope list is left out. A poll that is not approved throws ThalovantApiError with kind .deviceLoginPending(interval:), .deviceLoginExpired or .deviceLoginDenied, so every api-errors field stays on it and an existing catch still matches; revoking the token in use is idempotent (a 401 counts as revoked). loginWithBrowser runs on the same steps and still throws ThalovantDeviceLoginError. Run against the shared device-login vectors over URLSession, each exchange served and checked by a URLProtocol. Since 0.10.1: beginDeviceLogin(scopes:clientName:clientId:) and DeviceLoginOptions.clientId send client_id when given (homeAssistantClientId is Home Assistant's), and describeDeviceLogin(userCode:) reads GET /v1/auth/device/codes/{user_code} into DeviceLoginRequest, clientVerified only with a clientId.

home-link.reason: Sources/ThalovantSDK/HomeLink.swift: replyContext (no destination without a source), ThalovantClient.reply, HomeRequest, HomeAnswer, plainSpeech (stripSsml in Events.swift for real markup only, the portable reference set, Unicode White_Space) and answerHomeRequest(s), bounded by the hub's 10 s from arrival: the handler runs on a task of its own raced against its deadline, the answer goes out then whatever the handler does, and a reply that cannot go out in time is withdrawn. Keeping the link: LinkSupervisor and HubSession.run() in Session.swift; LinkLifetime.closeRefuses and the socket seam in Transport.swift, which reads refusals (1000/1005/1008 during the handshake or within 750 ms, a code up to 250 ms late, a 401/403 upgrade) as ThalovantConnectionError kind .refused and follows a failed KK with one XX attempt inside the same connect; NoiseNegotiator in Noise.swift tells a wrong password (.refused) from a changed hub key (.keyChanged). Run against the shared home-link vectors through the real reply path, and against link-keeping-vectors.json: close and supervise as pure functions, handshake through HiveMindWSSTransport against an in-memory hub that records the Noise patterns. Since 0.10.1: a frame that decrypts after the handshake -- JSON, WIRE-1 binary, a chunk, the hub's HELLO -- makes a later close a drop (LinkLifetime.heardAuthenticatedFrame); a refusal as an XX handshake ends is the hub refusing the client's own key, still kind .refused but with clientKeyRejected, keyFolder and otherKeyFolder set, and after KK a plain refusal; LinkSupervisor gives up on it at once, reported by giveUpReason beside LinkDecision.giveUp(.refused), since neither public enum can take a case without breaking an exhaustive switch. The handshake cases run as a kept link connects: the handshake, then the settle window. The queued cases hold a real link's send path with another frame.

runtime.reason: Applicable public behavior is implemented and exercised by the named regression suites and shared fixtures. HiveMind #251/#252 only changes the Python upstream client dispatcher; this consumer uses native single-dispatch transports (MCP delegates to the Node SDK), or caller-owned frame parsing in embedded C. No Python HiveMind bus dependency or slave-protocol reinjection exists here. Python now requires fixed upstream 1.1.9a1 and removes its identity-based suppression; equal independent native frames remain distinct. Reply claim metadata follows the Python string-ID contract, with first-seen ordering, case-sensitive fallback stages and legacy unstamped success. Invalid non-string stamps are ignored. Embedded C exposes bounded extraction and claim classification while its caller retains ordered IDs. Since 0.9.2: a skill's own speak event may set data.meta[thalovantClaimedMetaKey] (ThalovantEvents.thalovantClaimedMetaKey, "thalovant_claimed") to the literal true to positively assert it genuinely answered from the shared fallback tier; ThalovantReply.claimed checks this across events first, still after the ok/handled/no-failure gate, so it can turn a would-be false into true but never rescue a failed or unhandled reply, and any other value or a missing key is inert. Additive: an unstamped reply is judged exactly as before. The check is scoped to the skill's own speak event only -- [ThalovantEvents.speak, ThalovantEvents.ovosUtteranceSpeak], never the wider mediaEvents set (which also includes a skill sound clip with no meaning as a claim) and never any other correlated event this reply happens to carry (e.g. ovos.utterance.handled); the reference digest moved to 841f3bbeec23 after CodeRabbit caught the original unscoped scan on the embedded-C and Node ports.
